clue.text: UKIP evenly split about cut for foreign manager

indicators.note: the two picked letters are split apart and placed about the next piece
evenly takes the second and fourth letters of the party's name

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A political party divided over an immigration-style question about a foreign football boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Jürgen Klopp is the German football manager who led Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Jürgen Klopp is a German football coach, an example of a foreign manager in English football.

clue.text: Beautiful woman initially keen to get up for fast food

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a babe is slang for an attractive woman

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An attractive woman eager to rise for a quick meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skewered or doner meat is a staple takeaway, an example of quick food.

clue.text: Old demon with disappearing boat fitting

indicators.note: disappearing means a letter goes from the word

parts.note: a warlock is a wizard, a demonic figure

explanation.surface: An ancient fiend vanishing along with a piece of boat hardware.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowlock, or US oarlock, is the fitting on a boat's gunwale that holds an oar.

clue.text: Irritation as game is cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: piquet is a card game for two

explanation.surface: Annoyance when a match is abandoned early.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is resentment from wounded pride, a synonym for irritation.

clue.text: A fast climber gets out anonymous message

indicators.note: the climbing plant gets on the outside, wrapping round the other pieces

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A mountaineer who climbs quickly emerges and passes on an unsigned note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' is the noun, the Lenten fast, not speedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine card is traditionally sent unsigned, so it is an anonymous message of love.

clue.text: Listened to Indian TV host

indicators.note: listened to means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: Vijay is a common Indian given name

explanation.surface: Heard an Indian television presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: A VJ, spelt out as a word, is a video jockey who presents music videos on television.

clue.text: Spooner identifies his surreptitious drink supply with facial impression

indicators.note: Spooner swaps the opening sounds of words, and here speaks of his own possession

parts.note: Spooner speaking of his own would say my
a hip flask is a discreet supply of drink

explanation.surface: A man names his hidden booze along with a face mould.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner would say 'my flask'; swapping the M and L sounds gives 'mife lask' turned into 'life mask', the F moving across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast taken from a living person's face is a plaster impression of the face.

clue.text: Fasten damaged footwear, getting rid of black lubricating oil

indicators.note: damaged signals the letters are broken up and rearranged
getting rid of means a letter is removed

parts.note: a boot is footwear
B is the abbreviation for black on pencils

explanation.surface: Securing worn-out shoes, cleaned of dark polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatsfoot oil, rendered from cattle feet, is used to lubricate and soften leather.

clue.text: Line she scrawled describing her footwear

indicators.note: scrawled suggests messy writing, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sentence she has scribbled about her shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing high-heeled shoes is a description of what a woman has on her feet.

clue.text: Festival script includes your first payment schedule

indicators.note: includes means the next piece is placed inside

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the preceding word

parts.note: MS is manuscript, a script

explanation.surface: A holiday document contains your initial instalment.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying by instalments over time is a plan of payments, an arrangement schedule.

clue.text: Ship carrying nothing ornate

indicators.note: carrying means the vessel holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a barque is a sailing ship
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A vessel with no cargo described as elaborately decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: The baroque style of art and architecture is famously elaborate and heavily decorated.

clue.text: Displays trophy to sides in final

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters, taken from the word that follows

parts.note: the Ashes is the urn competed for in England-Australia cricket

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a cup to both teams at a final.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the trophy of England v Australia Test cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To flash something is to show it briefly, so flashes is a synonym for displays as a verb.

clue.text: Two guns satisfactory in causing injury

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a Bren is a light machine gun and an arm is a weapon, so the two give these letters
OK means satisfactory

explanation.surface: Two firearms in acceptable condition cause someone harm.
explanation.walkthrough: OK goes inside BREN, then ARM follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fractured limb above the hand is a common example of an injury.

clue.text: Nearly brush away first of the pudding

indicators.note: nearly means the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: to sweep is to brush away

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Almost clearing away the start of dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage sweet is a synonym for the dessert course of a meal.

clue.text: Diminutive child described by spots of a somewhat disreputable nature

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the spots enclose the next piece

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots

indicators.note: diminutive here means shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a kid is a child

explanation.surface: A small youngster covered in pimples seems a little shady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Described' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rakish means dashing but slightly dissolute, a synonym for somewhat disreputable.

clue.text: Understand the score about commercial — you don't want to face it!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an ad is a commercial

parts.words: you don't want to face it
parts.note: the idiom face the music means accept unpleasant consequences

explanation.surface: Grasping the situation about an advert you would rather avoid confronting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' is written music, not the situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand the notation of a written score is to be able to read it as a musician.

clue.text: Mistle-thrush finds mice, oddly, in street round Gibraltar?

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in places the picked letters inside the other pieces

parts.note: Gibraltar is known as the Rock

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bird finds rodents unusually in a road around the British territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormcock is an old country name for the mistle thrush, which sings in rough weather.

clue.text: Dictator stripped naked by employer's backer

indicators.note: stripped naked means the outer letters, the covering, are removed

parts.note: a despot is a dictator
a user is one who employs something; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A tyrant exposed by his boss's financial supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who espouses a cause supports it, so the word is a synonym for backer.

clue.text: Trap outlaw stealing first drink

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap

indicators.note: the opening letter is stolen, taken away from the front

parts.note: a bandit is an outlaw

explanation.surface: Catch a criminal pinching the first round at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Gin mixed with Italian vermouth is a classic cocktail, an example of a drink.

clue.text: Slav mother comes back to Iowa for delicious meal

indicators.note: comes back means the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a Sorb is a Slav of eastern Germany
ma is mother
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A Slavic mother returns to the Midwest for a tasty dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, hence anything delicious to eat.

clue.text: Mangled Belgian language

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Garbled speech from someone from Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the tongue of Bangladesh and West Bengal, an example of a language.

clue.text: Marshal rejected island's complaint

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Marshal Tito was the leader of Yugoslavia
IS is island, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A military leader turned away an island's grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Otitis is inflammation of the ear, and complaint means an ailment.

clue.text: Tore out article earlier in addition

indicators.note: earlier places the article before the rest

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: out means out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ripped out a piece of writing before.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereto is a formal word meaning besides or as well, a synonym for in addition.

clue.text: Part of group, don't forget, misses the first quarter

indicators.note: the first two of eight letters, a quarter, are missed off the front

parts.note: the request don't forget means remember

explanation.surface: A reminder that a band is short of its opening section.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone belonging to a club or society is one component of the group.

clue.text: Measure freedom in important cases

indicators.note: cases means encases, so the words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A gauge of liberty in significant legal matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cases' is a verb, not the legal noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a small unit of liquid measure, about a drop.

clue.text: See the consequence of state getting silver in a pretty normal way

indicators.note: a consequence follows, so the bishop's see comes after the rest

parts.note: to aver is to state
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Watch what happens when a nation acquires silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is the diocese of a bishop, not the verb; Ely is in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Averagely means in an ordinary, middling manner, a synonym for pretty normally.

clue.text: French departmental capital embarrassed internally

indicators.note: internally means the letters lie inside the word

explanation.surface: A French regional centre felt humiliated within.
explanation.definitionFit: Arras is the chief town of the Pas-de-Calais department in northern France.

clue.text: Russian bovine essentially mute

parts.note: a yak is a Himalayan bovine animal

indicators.note: essentially takes the core, the middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Russian ox is basically silent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yakuts are a Turkic people of Siberia in Russia, so a member is one kind of Russian.

clue.text: Sort of cocktail of soda mixed with drug

indicators.note: mixed signals the letters are stirred into a new order, as drinks are

parts.note: E is ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A drinks recipe: soda combined with a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn or seafood cocktail is a starter dish, so this is one kind of cocktail.

clue.text: Frenzied idiot goes round Queen's

indicators.note: goes round means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: berk is British slang for an idiot
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina, plus S for the 's

explanation.surface: A fool circles the monarch's property in a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Berserk means wildly out of control, a synonym for frenzied.

clue.text: May possibly credit conspiracy theorist with talking extremely rationally to begin with

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
David Icke is a well-known British conspiracy theorist

indicators.note: to begin with takes the first letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: Maybe give a conspiracy theorist credit for speaking very sensibly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' is Peter May, the England batsman and captain, not the month or verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter May captained England at cricket, so May is an example of one who plays the game.

clue.text: Drunken type somewhat lacking

definitions.meaning: a kind of drink taken, a small measure of spirits
a little deficient, as in being low on funds

explanation.definitionFit: A short is a spirit served in a small glass, and short also means insufficient.
